previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease, was admitted for a respiratory infection characterized by productive cough, fatigue, and low-grade fever. Testing revealed human metapneumovirus, and he was treated with azithromycin while IV cefepime was discontinued after clinical improvement. He received a platelet transfusion for epistaxis and thrombocytopenia, and one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia, with improvement in hemoglobin. His right great toe blister was managed with daily betadine dressings. His home medications were continued with adjustments, including holding pomalidomide and aspirin. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for oncology and podiatry.

EXAMINATION:  VENOUS DUP REFLUX BILAT

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with bilateral lower extremity swelling.// DVT?

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the bilateral lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation of the bilateral
common femoral, femoral, and popliteal veins.  Suboptimal visualization of the
calf veins, but where visualized appear patent.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

No evidence of medial popliteal fossa (___) cyst.  Severe subcutaneous edema
of bilateral calves.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the right or left lower extremity
veins.
2. Severe edema of the superficial soft tissues of bilateral calves.

EXAMINATION:  ULTRASOUND-GUIDED CORE NEEDLE BIOPSY

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with multiple myeloma, fluid retention, ___ on
CKD, concern for amyloidosis// soft tissue abdominal fat pad biopsy to
rule-out amyloidosis

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___

PROCEDURE:  Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy biopsy.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, radiology trainee and Dr. ___,
attending radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during
the key components of the procedure and reviewed and agrees with the trainee's
findings.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a supine position on the US scan table. Limited
preprocedure ultrasound of the anterior abdominal wall was performed.  Based
on the ultrasound findings an appropriate position for the biopsy was chosen. 
The site was marked.

The site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Approximately
___ cc of 1% lidocaine were administered to the subcutaneous and deep tissues
for local anesthetic effect.  Under continuous ultrasound guidance, an 18
gauge core biopsy device with a 22 mm throw was used to obtain two core biopsy
specimens, which were sent for pathology.


The procedure was tolerated well and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

FINDINGS: 

The right abdominal wall, at the level of the umbilicus, was targeted for
ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy as this was the area where the
subcutaneous fat was most prominent.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of anterior
abdominal wall subcutaneous fat.  Samples were submitted to pathology for
evaluation of possible amyloidosis.
